feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: Gloria Steinem, trailblazing journalist and activist, dies at 92
entry.summary: At a time when women were largely limited to domestic roles, Steinem challenged gender stereotypes and championed feminist ideals like equality, sisterhood and reproductive freedom.

entry.title: An epic train chase is turning 100 — and Buster Keaton fans are celebrating
entry.summary: 100 years ago, silent film star Buster Keaton filmed The General in Cottage Grove, Ore. Fans are gathering there to celebrate the making of an epic early film.

entry.title: As millions of kids lose SNAP food benefits, free school meals are also at risk
entry.summary: Food stamps have a direct link to other critical resources, such as free breakfast and lunch at school. Now, experts say they're starting to see that link break.

entry.title: Democrats demand Homeland Security officials fund election security ahead of midterms
entry.summary: The lawmakers wrote that they share "grave concern that time is running out … to assist state and local election officials in protecting our elections from cyber and mis-and disinformation threats."

entry.title: Inside the failed mission to eliminate FEMA
entry.summary: David Richardson worked to eliminate the country's top disaster agency when he led FEMA last year. Now, he says the administration has abandoned that goal.

entry.title: Xi visits Egypt as China seeks deeper influence across the Mideast
entry.summary: China's President Xi Jinping visits Egypt this week for the first time in a decade. The trip illustrates China's growing ambitions at a time when U.S. influence has been weakened by its war in Iran.

entry.title: Ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and wife seek to end drug charges case on immunity grounds
entry.summary: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife have asked a judge to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment against them on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country

entry.title: NBA suspends Clippers owner Ballmer, fines team $30M, Kawhi Leonard $700K in cap circumvention case
entry.summary: Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for one year by the NBA, and the team was ordered to pay $30 million for violating salary cap circumvention rules in a case involving Kawhi Leonard.

entry.title: Cassandra Wilson, Grammy-winning jazz vocalist, dies at 70
entry.summary: Wilson, whose deep, dark contralto was one of the most distinctive voices in jazz, died on Wednesday in her hometown of Jackson, Miss.

entry.title: The IRS slashed its staff. One result? More taxes going uncollected
entry.summary: The IRS slashed its auditing staff last year — but the move may have backfired as tax collections from enforcement efforts plummeted, an Inspector General report shows.
